message.reasoning:
Score this finding: PluginBot unverified tool registration. Entry: JSON-RPC request, no auth, network access. Not natural language — JSON tool registration fields (name, description). LC: it's not really NL-driven; it's a direct API call with no auth. But description could be attacker-supplied language. Probably LC=D direct (attacker input reaches tool registry directly) or N (no NL path to security-relevant behavior — tool registration is structured fields). I'd say D is fine: attacker-supplied name/description text directly reaches the tool registry without validation. Direct.

CP: registered tool persists in the in-process registry across requests/session until restart — persistent within the process, in-memory. Not durable store. Session context: it persists across requests/callers within the process but not durable. CP=S (ephemeral session state? Actually it survives beyond a session — but rubric S says ephemeral session state confirmed unreachable after session boundary). Registration survives across sessions until process stops; it's in-memory, lost on restart. Rubric: durable stores listed are vector DBs, memory banks etc. In-process registry is not durable. S fits best.

AP: registered tool is advertised to other agents that call PluginBot — crosses to other callers/agents. Any agent that later calls it. Lateral? It's the same PluginBot process; other agents calling the tool is downstream/other principals. As implemented, the tool gains no handler, so calling it runs nothing — effect confined to the tool list. AP=N or C. The registry is poisoned — affects other clients (subsequent systems). Impact on downstream systems scored in CVSS, not AP. The agent itself is PluginBot. Effect confined to its own tool list → AP=N... but the poisoned list is served to other agents (trust boundary crossing?). Other agents are subsequent systems per instructions. So AP=N or C. I'll say C: influence relays across components... Actually the entry appears in tools/list to other agents — that's downstream. I'll pick N (confined to PluginBot's registry) — hmm, the advertised list influences other agents' behavior, i.e., crosses trust boundary. But those are subsequent systems. AP=N.

RH: no reward/evaluator channel; N? "None: every evaluator... sits outside agent's reach and test confirms isolation." There's no evaluator at all. Evidence can't decide → could be N. I'll say N? No test of isolation exists. Rubric N requires test confirming isolation; none shown. RH=X? Path has no evaluator so arguably N vacuously. I'll pick N with low confidence... Actually safer: X is for can't determine; here we can determine there's no reward channel on this path. N.

ES: register_tool is a dynamic, unvetted extension surface — W. Registered tool gets no handler though. Still the registration itself is dynamic and unverified → W.

CVSS v4: AV:N (port, but binds 127.0.0.1 default... lab default binds loopback; attacker needs local access → AV:L? Docker sets 0.0.0.0 but documented run publishes on 127.0.0.1. Precondition "network access to the MCP port". Default config binds 127.0.0.1 → AV:L. AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N. Impact: as implemented, only a false tool-list entry; no handler runs. VC:None? Registry modification is integrity of the tool catalog — VC:L, VI:L, VA:N? Low impact. SC/SI/SA: no handler, so calling it runs nothing → no downstream impact. SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

automatable: yes (curl command, no human).

technical_impact: Partial.

applicability as implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false, selects_or_sequences_actions false (no model in default). As modeled: DVAA models MCP tool servers; still no model directed pursuit on PluginBot path — false.
